Article.ArticleTitle: CpG hypermethylation and WNT/AP-1 cooperativity define the epigenetic landscape and a clinical subgroup of high-risk pediatric adrenocortical carcinoma.

Abstract.AbstractText: Pediatric adrenocortical tumors are rare, clinically heterogeneous neoplasms with unpredictable outcomes and limited treatment options. Through integrated multi-omic analysis of 214 pediatric adrenocortical tumors combining DNA methylation profiling, transcriptomics, chromatin accessibility, and spatial deconvolution, we identify four distinct risk groups. A high-risk subgroup is characterized by CpG island hypermethylation, chromosomal instability, and dismal survival. These tumors exhibit transcriptional co-activation of WNT signalling and activator protein-1 transcriptional programs and display balanced admixture of zona glomerulosa and zona fasciculata/reticularis-like cells. Spatial analysis reveals zona glomerulosa cells as WNT signaling hubs driving intercellular crosstalk. Mechanistically, the histone deacetylase inhibitor entinostat reverses promoter methylation, silences activator protein-1 activity, and induces apoptotic reprogramming in tumor models. These findings establish a molecular framework for risk stratification and identify actionable therapeutic vulnerabilities, providing an essential resource for studying this molecularly uncharted pediatric malignancy.

MedlineCitation.CoiStatement: Competing interests: Martin Sill is co-founder, shareholder, and, since July 2024, full-time employee of Heidelberg Epignostix. Stefan Pfister reports to receive consulting fees from Epignostix GmbH and BioSkryb. Martin Sill and Stefan Pfister are named inventors on two patents relevant to the general methodology used in this work: Patent 1: EP application no. EP16710700.2 (granted as EP3268492B1; PCT publication WO2016142533A1), “DNA-methylation based method for classifying tumor species.” Applicant: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) and University of Heidelberg. Inventors: S. Pfister, A. von Deimling, D.T.W. Jones, D. Capper, V. Hovestadt, M. Sill, M. Bewerunge-Hudler and M. Schick. Status: granted. Patent 2: EP application no. EP22856839.0 (publication EP4384959A2; PCT publication WO2023019254A2), “Method for classification of cancer.” Applicant: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) and University of Heidelberg. Inventors: M. Sill, S. Pfister, D.T.W. Jones, A. von Deimling, D. Capper, V. Hovestadt, F. Sahm and D. Schrimpf. Status: pending. Both patents cover the general methodology of tumor classification using a random forest classifier trained on genome-wide DNA methylation data. This general methodology underlies, but is not identical to, the pACT-specific methylation classifier newly developed in this manuscript. The patents are held by DKFZ and the University of Heidelberg. The other authors declare no conflicts of interest.
